name: Sarah Sowden
bio:
Dr Sarah Sowden MA(oxf) MPH PhD FFPH FHEA is a Clinical Senior Lecturer and Honorary Consultant in Public Health. Her career is dedicated to improving health and care equity and to developing future generations of practitioner-academics equipped with the skills, capability and capacity to create better health and improved care for all. Her work sits at the intersection of research leadership, workforce development and system-wide collaboration, building people, programmes and partnerships with a strong commitment to inclusive, supportive and high-performing environments. 

The research team she leads focuses on reducing health and care inequalities, with 41 peer-reviewed publications (21 as lead or senior author) and £31.3m in total research income (>£7.4m directly attributable) while working part-time since 2020. My Deep End and UNFAIR research programmes have shaped NHS England national inequalities work, and underpinned a £6m NHS Integrated Care Board investment in our region into Deep End network activity to address health and care inequalities, which contributed to the government’s 10‑year health plan, and was cited as one of the top 5 impact successes across the National Institute for Health and Care Research (NIHR) Applied Research Collaborations nationally. 

She brings experience of national infrastructure leadership as Deputy Director of the £22m NIHR Research Support Service Specialist Centre for Public Health delivered by Newcastle University and partners, where she co-leads a national platform that strengthens research capacity in public health, oversee more than £5m direct investment into local government research practitioner posts, and shape national approaches to research culture, governance and 
capability development.
